the enrichment design of the SONAR trial will be used to identify individuals with diabetes and albuminuric CKD most likely to respond to atrasentan, a novel selective endothelin A antagonist.

the development of new treatments for diabetic nephropathy and the design of clinical trials to test these treatments.
the development and evaluation of novel therapeutic strategies for patients with diabetic nephropathy and the prevention of progression of kidney disease.

the design and implementation of clinical trials of novel interventions in diabetic nephropathy, with the aim to reduce the number of patients required for trials, and the time and cost of their implementation, while improving the chance of success.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the SONAR study design, which uses a biomarker to identify the patients who are more likely to respond to the treatment and therefore to benefit from it, is a novel and potentially powerful approach to clinical trial design.
atrasentan is effective in reducing albuminuria and may be effective in reducing renal events in a subgroup of patients with diabetic nephropathy and albuminuria.

we have shown the feasibility of an enrichment design for the treatment of patients with diabetic nephropathy and that the design is likely to be more effective in identifying patients who respond to treatment.
